targets.authors: Pessiglione, M., Petrovic, P., Daunizeau, J., Palminteri, S., Dolan, R. J., & Frith, C. D.
targets.title: Subliminal instrumental conditioning demonstrated in the human brain.
targets.evidence_quote: Here, we attempt to replicate the original result of Pessiglione et al. (2008), leveraging the developments in the field of unconscious processing to apply a more robust statistical approach (Experiment 1), and a more rigorous methodology (Experiment 2).
targets.outcome_quote: We find that learning took place when replicating the original methods directly (albeit we could not assert that the full sample was unaware in the separate awareness check, PDT2). However, following the enhancement of the sensitivity of the thresholdsetting perceptual discrimination task, and the introduction of a trial-by-trial awareness check permitting exclusion of individual trials, we found evidence for the absence of learning. All conclusions were based on informed Bayes factors.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The direct replication obtains the learning effect, but the main message is that original awareness methods cannot establish unconscious learning; improved awareness detection removes the effect. The methodological critique is central, warranting the special flawed category. Mixed is a plausible alternative under the rule for direct versus conceptual attempts, and failed under the final substantive rejection of unconscious learning; this categorical ambiguity lowers confidence.

reasoning: Two new experiments re-test one published paper. The paper is the completed Stage 2 article, not the earlier Stage 1 plan. Earlier and concurrent conditioning studies are background corroboration, not additional targets. Recalculating a Bayes factor from reported summary statistics does not make the new-sample experiments a reproduction of original raw data.
